title: One Second, Sliced
log: The recording leaves the screen and becomes a flip book of 120 real frames on glass slabs. Then one second is laid out as 120 boxes you can count, and one of them opens into 6.3 ms of work in an 8.3 ms slot.
wow: The 120 boxes arrive in exactly one second. On "eight" one turns amber and opens up, and while Helen says it, the work fills 6.3 of its 8.3 ms. At the end one frame slides out of the stack like a card from a deck.
fit: It turns an engineering number (6 ms of work in an 8 ms slot) into something anyone can see. Strong for developers.

title: The Frustrated Postman

wow: 'A very frustrated postman': arms up, eyes go > <, steam from his cap, while the sealed letters keep sailing past him.
fit: The hardest security claim in the product (the server never carries plaintext) as a story a child understands. A character Roomler could keep.

title: The Daemon, Exploded
log: A machined hexagonal puck opens. Its plates slide out like drawers and fly into a honeycomb of five screens, the five jobs of one daemon, then slam back into one object.
wow: The hard mechanical slam: five screens fly back into the puck in a third of a second, and it is one small object again.
fit: 'One daemon per machine' is the architecture's invariant and the reason it is one install, shown like hardware.

title: Across Town
kind: Warm story that turns into scale

wow: One unbroken camera move from a driveway to the whole Earth: the town really sits on the globe.
fit: The families-helping-families story and the private mesh, in one shot. The warmest demo here: for Facebook and non-technical people.

title: Remote Inception
log: A remote desktop inside a remote desktop inside a remote desktop, for ever: MacBook, Windows laptop, Mac mini on Linux, MacBook.
wow: There is no last frame. The camera dives for ever and the film loops with no seam. Measured on the finished file, the step across the seam (SSIM 0.751) is the same as a normal step between two frames (0.750).
fit: 'Any machine, from any browser' as a hypnotic loop, with real recordings on every screen. Made to autoplay muted.

title: Hex-Flip Trailer
kind: Trailer and a reusable transition pack
log: The six-minute podcast cut down to its best lines, glued by Roomler's own transition: the frame turns into hexagons that flip in a wave and carry the next clip on their backs.
wow: The hex wave passing over a talking head and leaving the next scene behind it, in the logo's own shape.
fit: This is the 'glue' you asked for, and it scales: the transitions are a pack that any future video can use with one command.
blender: The hex-flip wave, slabs falling away and a fold, all rendered from the cut's own frames (emission only, no denoiser)
